facts.fact: Siddhendra Yogi shaped Kuchipudi.
Kuchipudi was traditionally performed only by men.
Bhamakalapam (on Satyabhama) is the signature Kuchipudi item.
Tholu Bommalata is leather shadow-puppet theatre.
Burrakatha evolved from Jangam Katha.
Adibhatla Narayana Das pioneered Harikatha in Telugu.
Oggu Katha is the Saiva ballad of the Yadava Oggu priests.
Nrittaratnavali was written by Jayapa Senani at the Kakatiya court.
Kondapalli toys are carved from soft Punki wood.
Etikoppaka toys are lac-turned Ankudu wood.
Budithi (Srikakulam) is known for bell-metal and brass ware.
Bobbili (Vizianagaram) makes the veena from a single jackwood log.
Udayagiri (Nellore) is known for wooden cutlery.
Srikalahasti Kalamkari is free-hand pen work.
Machilipatnam Kalamkari is block-printed.
Dharmavaram is known for silk sarees with gold borders.
Venkatagiri is known for fine cotton sarees.
Mangalagiri is known for cotton sarees with Nizam border.
The telia-rumal ikat technique is traced to Chirala.
Pochampally Ikat is a Telangana GI.
Banaganapalle mangoes got the GI tag in 2017.
Tirupati Laddu got the GI tag in 2009.
The first complete Telugu inscription (c. 575 CE) is of the Renati Cholas.
It was found at Erragudipadu (Kadapa).
The Kavitrayam are Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.
Allasani Peddana wrote Manu Charitramu.
Annamayya is the pada kavita pitamaha.
Kshetrayya addressed his padams to Muvva Gopala.
Vemana wrote the Vemana Satakam.
Kandukuri Veeresalingam wrote the first Telugu novel.
Gurajada Apparao wrote Kanyasulkam.
Gidugu Ramamurthy championed spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu.
Ayaka pillars are unique to Andhra stupas.
Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was the Ikshvaku centre.
The Undavalli caves are Vishnukundi works.
Lepakshi Virabhadra temple is a Vijayanagara work with a hanging pillar.
The Gudimallam lingam is among the earliest anthropomorphic lingas.
Srisailam is both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha.
Srikalahasti has the Vayu linga.
Ahobilam has nine Narasimha shrines.
Ugadi is the Telugu New Year.
Ponduru khadi got the GI tag in December 2025.
Nandamuri Balakrishna received the Padma Bhushan in 2025.
Kuchipudi village lies in Movva mandal of Krishna district.
Vempati Chinna Satyam founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras (1963).
Yamini Krishnamurthy, the Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi star, was born at Madanapalle.
Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was famed for playing female roles (Satyabhama) in Kuchipudi.
Nataraja Ramakrishna revived Perini Sivatandavam and the temple dance called Andhra Natyam.
Perini Sivatandavam, the 'dance of warriors', comes from the Kakatiya age (described in Jayapa's Nrittaratnavali).
Tappeta Gullu is a drum dance of Srikakulam–Vizianagaram performed to invoke rain.
Butta Bommalu (West Godavari) is danced wearing large basket-made masks.
Dappu is the vigorous frame-drum dance of Andhra.
Garagalu is a pot-balancing dance of the Godavari districts.
The Lambadi dance is performed by the Banjara (Lambada) tribe.
Gobbi is danced by girls around cow-dung balls during Sankranti.
Nimmalakunta (Sri Sathya Sai district) is the leather-puppet village; Dalavai Chalapathi Rao got the Padma Shri (2020).
Shaik Nazar is the 'father of modern Burrakatha'.
Tallapaka Annamacharya composed about 32,000 sankirtanas on Lord Venkateswara.
Bhadrachala Ramadas (Kancharla Gopanna) was a tahsildar of Tana Shah who built the Bhadrachalam temple.
Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna, the Carnatic maestro, was born at Sankaraguptam (East Godavari).
AP's state song 'Maa Telugu Talliki' was written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari.
Nannaya wrote the first Telugu grammar, Andhra Shabda Chintamani (in Sanskrit).
Tikkana is called 'Kavi Brahma'; Errana 'Prabandha Parameswara'.
Nannechoda wrote the Kumarasambhavamu in jaanu Telugu.
Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranamu in dwipada metre.
Srinatha, court poet of Pedakomati Vema Reddi, wrote Sringara Naishadhamu.
Bammera Potana refused to dedicate his Bhagavatam to any king.
Nandi Timmana wrote Parijatapaharanamu.
Dhurjati wrote the Kalahasteeswara Satakamu.
Madayyagari Mallana wrote Rajasekhara Charitramu.
Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu wrote Ramabhyudayamu.
Pingali Surana wrote Kalapurnodayamu and Raghava Pandaviyamu.
Ramarajabhushana (Bhattumurthy) wrote Vasucharitramu.
Tenali Ramakrishna wrote Panduranga Mahatyamu.
Krishnadevaraya ('Andhra Bhoja') wrote 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' in Amuktamalyada.
Telugu was called the 'Italian of the East' (Niccolo de' Conti).
C.P. Brown compiled a Telugu–English dictionary and published Vemana's verses.
Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitramu (1878) is the first Telugu novel; he ran the journal Viveka Vardhini.
29 August, Gidugu Ramamurthy's birthday, is Telugu Language Day.
Sri Sri wrote Maha Prasthanam (1950).
Gurram Jashuva wrote Gabbilam.
Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote the reformist novel Malapalli.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the Jnanpith (1970) for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu.
C. Narayana Reddy won the Jnanpith (1988) for Viswambhara.
Ravuri Bharadwaja won the Jnanpith (2012) for Paakudu Raallu.
Kondapalli Bommallu received the GI tag in 2007.
Etikoppaka toys received the GI tag in 2017.
Bandar (Machilipatnam) Laddu received the GI tag in 2017.
Araku Valley Arabica Coffee received the GI tag in 2019.
Uppada Jamdani sarees received the GI tag in 2009.
The Bobbili Veena received the GI tag in 2011.
Durgi (Palnadu) is known for GI-tagged stone carvings.
Narsapur (West Godavari) is known for GI-tagged crochet lace.
Tirupati wooden toys are carved from red sanders (raktachandan).
The Ambari Hathi (elephant with howdah) is a famous Kondapalli toy.
Kalamkari takes its name from 'kalam' (pen) and 'kari' (craftwork).
Machilipatnam-style block-printed Kalamkari is made at Pedana.
Nirmal toys and paintings are Telangana GIs, not Andhra Pradesh.
Nagarjunakonda is named after Acharya Nagarjuna, founder of the Madhyamika school.
The Nagarjunakonda remains were moved to an island museum when the Nagarjuna Sagar dam flooded the valley.
Salihundam (Srikakulam) is a Buddhist site on the Vamsadhara.
Thotlakonda and Bavikonda are hill-top Buddhist monasteries near Visakhapatnam.
Sankaram (Bojjannakonda) near Anakapalli has rock-cut Buddhist stupas and caves.
Ghantasala (Krishna) was a Buddhist port-town (Kantakossyla of Ptolemy).
Many Amaravati sculptures are in the British Museum and the Government Museum, Chennai.
The five Pancharamas are Amaravati, Draksharamam, Samarlakota, Palakollu and Bhimavaram.
Lepakshi was built by the brothers Virupanna and Viranna under Achyuta Deva Raya (1530s).
The monolithic Nandi at Lepakshi is among the largest in India.
Mukhalingam (Srikakulam) has the Eastern Ganga Madhukeswara temple.
The Arasavalli Sun temple (Srikakulam) is one of India's few living Sun temples.
Srikurmam has the only temple of Vishnu as Kurma (tortoise).
The gold-plated vimana over the Tirumala sanctum is the Ananda Nilayam.
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) was constituted in 1932.
Yaganti (Nandyal) is famed for its Uma Maheswara temple and its "growing" Nandi.
Kanipakam (Chittoor) has the Varasiddhi Vinayaka temple.
At Simhachalam the sandal paste is removed from the deity once a year on Akshaya Tritiya (Chandanotsavam).
Tadipatri has the Vijayanagara-era Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples.
The Kanaka Durga temple of Vijayawada stands on the Indrakeeladri hill.
The three days of Sankranti are Bhogi, Sankranti and Kanuma.
Atla Taddi is a women's festival of Andhra in Ashvayuja month.
The Rottela Panduga (bread festival) is held at the Bara Shaheed Dargah, Nellore, during Muharram.
The Tatayyagunta Gangamma Jatara is the folk festival of Tirupati.
The Flamingo Festival is held at Pulicat Lake (Sullurpeta, Tirupati district).
Bonalu and Bathukamma are Telangana festivals.
